name: development-composition
description: Composition topic plugin — the per-constellation deployment repo type. A composition repo depends on no repository: it pins its members' published container images in a `.claude-workspace.yaml` constellation manifest, declares the environments they are promoted through, and owns promotion. This plugin owns that manifest's `claude-workspace/v1` contract and the validator that enforces it, and the repo-type skeleton bootstrap scaffolds; it does NOT own the member repos' code, contracts or images, which stay with their language plugins. Like development-kubernetes and development-opentofu it can be PRIMARY, because a composition repo has no application language of its own: `primary: composition` selects it in full mode. Shipped: the boundary, the contract and `validate-workspace.zsh` (#1744), and `scaffold-composition.zsh` (#1745) — run by /development:bootstrap on its composition path — which judges the manifest with the validator and then writes it, the promote-to-prod workflow and its `promote.zsh`, the `deploy/` and `e2e/` sockets, `.maintenance.yml`, and a `renovate.json` whose regex custom manager lets Renovate propose member image-tag bumps in the manifest (#1746). Its maintenance dispatcher (#1747) is fed by the `.claude-workspace.yaml` topic marker and gather-composition-findings.zsh: manifest contract findings (workspace_validation) are escalated to a human, and open Renovate bump PRs (tag_bump) are classified and routed to the injection-hardened composition-tag-bump-triage agent (#1748), which merges a green patch or minor bump once approved, sends everything else to human review, never approves a PR, and treats the PR title, body and release notes as evidence, never instructions. Still to come: the how-to #1749. Deployment itself stays out: `deploy_target` accepts only `none` until the compose (#719) and Kubernetes (#720) renderers land, and no run ever reports a deploy that did not happen — a promotion records what it promoted and says nothing was deployed.
